elicitation_input.question: In the United Kingdom, what is the average age of onset for alcohol related dementia?
elicitation_input.question_type: Directed question that has a single unambiguous answer

llm_generation.text:
In the UK, alcohol-related dementia is usually considered a **younger-onset dementia**. The average age at presentation/onset is commonly reported as **around 55 years**, with many cases occurring between **about 45 and 65 years**.

Some UK clinical and charity sources describe alcohol-related brain damage/dementia as most often affecting people in their **40s to 50s**, and it is substantially more common before age 65 than most other dementia types. Exact averages vary because diagnoses are inconsistent and symptoms may develop gradually after years of heavy drinking, nutritional deficiency—especially thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency—and repeated withdrawal or illness.

Importantly, alcohol-related cognitive impairment can sometimes **partly improve** with sustained abstinence, good nutrition, thiamine treatment, and support—unlike many progressive neurodegenerative dementias.
